story.headline: Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth, NASA says
story.summary: NASA's Voyager 1, launched in 1977, reached a distance of one light-day from Earth, about 16 billion miles, at 5:16 a.m. EST on Nov. 18. It is the first human-made object to get that far, so a radio command now takes 24 hours to reach the probe and another 24 hours for a reply to come back.

quote.text: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is now one light-day from Earth — so far away that it takes signals a full 24 hours to reach the probe.

story.headline: Hannah Lillith Assadi's 'Paradiso 17' wins the 2026 National Book Award for fiction in New York
story.summary: Hannah Lillith Assadi won the National Book Award for fiction for 'Paradiso 17', her novel about a Palestinian exile, at the National Book Awards ceremony in New York City on Nov. 18. Abdelrahman ElGendy's memoir 'Huna' won the nonfiction prize. ElGendy, who was denied a U.S. visa, according to the National Book Foundation, was represented at the ceremony by his editor, who accepted the award.

quote.text: Hannah Lillith Assadi’s “Paradiso 17,” a loving, melancholy and poetic account of a Palestinian exile’s worldwide journey, won the National Book Award for fiction.

story.headline: Mass General Brigham patient passes one year with a gene-edited pig kidney, the longest on record
story.summary: Molly Falco, 58, of New Hampshire, reached one year on Nov. 22 with a genetically modified pig kidney transplanted at Mass General Brigham in Boston. According to The New York Times, no other patient is known to have lived longer with a pig kidney, and she has not been hospitalized since February. A 33-patient clinical trial of the kidneys is planned for January.

quote.text: The patient, Molly Falco, a mother of two who has worked as a chef, has lived with a kidney from a genetically modified pig for longer than any other patient is known to have so far.
